newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound up on dollar in week.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound up on dollar in week.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued to rise against the dollar in the week ended on Thursday, and dealers said there was heavy supply of U.S. currency during the the four working days.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,538-1,547.5 pounds per dollar from 1,538.5-1,548 and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.

Shadi Hanna, Treasurer at Byblos Bank, said the dollar's supply was high and trade was restricted to a tight range of 75 piasters at the bid end of the intervention band, putting it at 1,538.25-1,539.
Last week the dollar closed at 1,538.5-1,539 pound in interbank trading.
"All demand for dollars was met by commercial banks and the Central Bank bought between $5 million to $10 million," Hanna told Reuters.
Markets will be closed on Friday for Moslem Ashoura holiday.
